note_tweet.text:
We all saw who had it first.

Ronaldo was the more natural free-kick taker than Messi. Messi had to practice for years to catch up.

Ronaldo was scoring free-kicks at night when Messi was nowhere to be found. Go and watch the early years. Manchester United, early Madrid - every dead ball felt like a goal. Knuckleball. Curl. Top corner. Keepers frozen.

Fast forward to the end of their careers, Ronaldo stops scoring them and Messi starts scoring more. And somehow the media tries to sell us the narrative of "hard work vs natural talent."

In my judgement, what I call natural is what you can do efficiently at a young age without having to learn it for 15 years. Not what took another person 15 years to perfect to start catching up.

Practice makes perfect, and the one that continues practicing will always outlast the one who excelled with talent. Because when you are talented at something, you take it for granted.

Ronaldo was born with it. The free-kick was his weapon from day one. He didn't need to learn it - he owned it.

Messi had to work for it, and I respect that. But let's not rewrite history. Natural is natural.
